banners.cannotPlay: Clips cannot play inside this window.
banners.notRecordingHelp: Gloaming keeps retrying on its own. If it is an encoder problem, a reboot after a driver update usually clears it, or pick a different encoder under Settings, Recording.
banners.cpuFallbackHelp: Your GPU encoder would not open, so Gloaming fell back to CPU encoding to keep clipping. That costs frames in games. This is usually a driver that needs a reboot after an update. Gloaming tries the GPU first every time it starts, so once that is sorted this goes away on its own.
banners.codecFallbackHelp: Your GPU would not encode the codec picked under Settings, Recording, so gpu-screen-recorder chose one it can handle. Recording is still on the GPU and clips are unaffected. Choosing a different encoder yourself stops this notice, and H.264 in particular tops out at 4096 pixels wide on NVIDIA, so HEVC or AV1 is the one to pick on a wide monitor.
banners.cannotPlayHelp: The installed Qt WebEngine build has no H.264 decoder. Recording still works, and clips open fine in your system player. To fix in-app playback, install your distro's WebEngine package and reinstall Gloaming:
banners.cpuFallbackNvencApi: Your NVIDIA driver supports NVENC {driver}, but the FFmpeg on this system needs {required}, so the GPU encoder cannot open. That costs frames in games, and a reboot will not fix it. Recording on the GPU again needs a newer NVIDIA driver, or an FFmpeg built for NVENC {driver} if your card does not get newer drivers.
banners.nvencUseFlatpak: The Flatpak gpu-screen-recorder is installed and works with this driver: choose it under Settings, Recording.
banners.nvencGetFlatpak: The Flatpak gpu-screen-recorder works with this driver. Install it with {command}, then choose it under Settings, Recording.

tutorial.startClipping: Start clipping, then let Gloaming run
tutorial.colourBody: Gloaming takes its colour from one of these. The whole window changes as you pick, so choose the one you want to look at, and change it any time in Settings.
tutorial.quickStartBody: Gloaming keeps the buffer live in the background and opens this window only when you need it.
tutorial.playlistsBody: Every clip can live in any number of playlists, and they keep themselves in order.
tutorial.sessionHelp: Double-tap to start or stop a full recording. Tap once during a session to mark a highlight.
tutorial.reviewHelp: Open any clip to rename it, trim the best moment, share a link, or press H to add highlights.
tutorial.backgroundHelp: Minimize or close this window and Gloaming keeps recording. Discord Rich Presence is on by default and lives in Settings.
tutorial.autoHelp: Clips are filed under the game you were playing when you saved them. Gloaming builds these on its own.
tutorial.customHelp: Create your own from the sidebar, pick an emoji and a colour, then drag clips onto it or right-click a clip to add it.
tutorial.safeHelp: Playlists follow clips through renames and trims, and tidy up after deletions.
tutorial.bufferTitle: How far back Gloaming can reach
tutorial.bufferBody: Gloaming is always recording into a buffer it throws away. Pressing the clip key keeps the last stretch of it, and this is how long that stretch is.
tutorial.bufferNote: The buffer holds {buffer} at a time. A longer one costs memory, and Settings has the whole picture, including writing it to disk instead.
tutorial.screenshotKeyNote: The screenshot key is unset until you set one. It saves a picture of the screen to the Images section and puts it on your clipboard.
tutorial.editorHelp: Put several clips on a timeline, cut them together, add text and transitions, and export one video. It is in the sidebar.
tutorial.shareBody: Every clip has a link, and copying it is one button on the card.
tutorial.linkHelp: The link button on a clip copies an address that plays the clip in a browser. Paste it into Discord and it embeds.
tutorial.tunnelHelp: On its own the link only works on this machine. Turn on the Cloudflare tunnel in Settings and it works anywhere, until the daemon restarts and the address changes.
tutorial.moreBody: That is everything you need. Settings has the parts you only touch once.
tutorial.recHelp: Encoder, resolution, frame rate, which monitor, and which audio goes on which track.
tutorial.gameCaptureHelp: Game Capture records just the game's window, so Discord and other windows stay out of your clips. Off records the whole display. You can switch it any time from quick settings.
tutorial.shareDiscordHelp: Off, the Share button copies a link. On, it copies the clip itself, shrunk to fit Discord's free upload limit. Right-click Share for the other one, and change it any time in Settings.

accents.customBody: Pick any colour and Gloaming builds a full Material 3 scheme from it. Only the hue carries over: the surfaces, the buttons and the text tones are worked out from it, the same way the five presets are.
accents.lowContrast: This colour does not leave enough contrast to read comfortably. Gloaming has lightened the accent as far as it can; try something less dark.

settings.padOverlayKeyHelp: Show or hide the controller overlay with a keyboard shortcut, including while in a game.
settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Tune Gloaming to the way you play
settings.bufferOnDisk: Buffer is kept on disk, so long durations are fine.
settings.bufferPlain: Seconds of gameplay kept in the rolling buffer
settings.bufferRamWarning: A {length} buffer in RAM uses roughly {gb} GB at typical bitrates. Auto storage moves it to disk.
settings.replayStorageHelp: Where the rolling buffer lives. Auto keeps short buffers in RAM and moves anything over ten minutes to disk.
settings.clipDurationHelp: Seconds saved when you press the clip key
settings.gsrSourceHelp: The Flatpak build carries its own FFmpeg, which still records on the GPU with older NVIDIA drivers that your system's FFmpeg no longer supports.
settings.keyOverlayHelp: Shows the keys you press in a small panel over your game, so they are in your recording and your stream. Only the keys on the panel are read.
settings.keyOverlayPositionHelp: Pick a corner, or press Move it and drag the panel where you want it.
settings.keyOverlayKeyHelp: Shows or hides the overlay without opening Gloaming.
settings.keyOverlayKeyNow: {key} now shows and hides the overlay
settings.keyOverlayInClipsHelp: Saves which of the overlay's keys you pressed during each clip, so the viewer can show them later even if the overlay was off. Nothing else you type is kept.
settings.errSaveOverlay: Could not save the overlay setting
settings.overlayNoLayerShell: The overlay needs layer-shell or an available XWayland display. On GNOME, enable XWayland and restart Gloaming.
settings.overlayNoGtk: The overlay needs GTK 3 and gtk-layer-shell for Python. On Arch install gtk-layer-shell and python-gobject; on Debian and Ubuntu gir1.2-gtklayershell-0.1 and python3-gi-cairo.
settings.overlayNoDisplay: Gloaming could not find your desktop session to show the overlay on.
settings.overlayCrashed: The overlay keeps closing. gloaming.log has the reason.
settings.typeExact: {label}: click to type an exact number of seconds
settings.customResolutionWarn: Write it as width by height, like 1600x900.
settings.badResolutionTitle: That resolution is not a size
settings.badResolutionDetail: Write it as width by height, like 1600x900
settings.containerHelp: MKV survives crashes better and suits multi-track audio. Discord embeds and browsers need MP4.
settings.encoderHelp: GPU encoders are faster and use less CPU. Vulkan options require the gpu-screen-recorder backend.
settings.colourDepthHelp: 8-bit suits every player. 10-bit needs an HEVC or AV1 encoder.
settings.hardwareDecodeHelp: Let your GPU decode clips in this window instead of the CPU. Worth turning on if high-resolution AV1 or HEVC previews stutter. It renders video black on some drivers, so if that happens turn it back off. Takes effect next time you open Gloaming.
settings.followMouseHelp: Record whichever monitor the pointer is on. Switching monitors restarts the buffer, so a clip taken right after moving will be short.
settings.followMouseUnsupported: Needs X11, Hyprland or Sway. Gloaming cannot tell where the pointer is on this session.
settings.windowCaptureHelp: Record only the focused game's window instead of the whole display. Only windows Gloaming recognizes as a game count, so alt-tabbing to Discord or a browser does not move the capture. Switching to a different game restarts the buffer, so a clip taken right after is short.
settings.windowCaptureWayland: Not supported on Wayland: gpu-screen-recorder can't capture a single game window here, so this records the whole display.
settings.windowCaptureTools: Install xdotool and xprop so Gloaming can detect the focused game.
settings.windowCaptureFailed: Gloaming couldn't pin the recording to your game's window, so it is recording the whole display.
settings.displayMissing: Display "{id}" is not being reported right now. It is still saved and will be used if it comes back.
settings.displayNone: No individual displays were detected. Auto will still work.
settings.displayHelp: Choose which display to record. Auto follows the backend default.
settings.captureMicHelp: Record your mic into clips. The same switch as the tile on Home, and saved the moment you flip it.
settings.errMic: Could not change the microphone setting
settings.desktopSourceIsMic: This is a microphone input, so clips would have no desktop audio. Pick one under Desktop audio instead.
settings.desktopSourceMissing: That source is not listed right now. It is still saved and will be passed to the recorder.
settings.desktopSourceHelp: Choose what the recorder captures as desktop audio.
settings.micSourceHelp: Used when mic capture is on. Default input follows the system setting.
settings.micMonoHelp: Centres your mic in the clip. Turn this on if your voice only comes out of one ear, which is what most XLR and single-channel interfaces do. Applied when the clip is saved, so it needs mic capture on and no separate audio tracks.
settings.desktopVolumeHelp: Balanced into new clips as they are saved
settings.micVolumeHelp: Turn this down if your mic overpowers the game. Applies while mic capture is on.
settings.notifyVolumeHelp: The ping when a clip is saved, and the session start, stop and highlight tones.
settings.customSoundsHelp: Play your own file instead of the built-in tone. Leave blank for the tone. A path that does not exist falls back to the tone, so you never end up with silence.
settings.audioTracksHelp: Output 1 follows your main audio selection. Enable Output 2 or 3 only when needed; the microphone has its own controls.
settings.duplicateTrack: That source is already a track
settings.mixFirstTrackHelp: Record an extra track 1 that mixes every source, so players and shared clips carry full audio. Your separate tracks start at 2.
settings.wfMicModeHelp: How wf-recorder handles desktop audio together with a microphone
settings.wfMicTitle: How should the microphone be mixed in?
settings.wfMicBody: wf-recorder records one audio source at a time. Choose what happens when both the desktop and the microphone are on.
settings.wfMicChoiceBoth: Use a backend that can do both
settings.wfMicChoiceBothBody: Gloaming records with a compatible backend whenever the microphone is on.
settings.wfMicChoiceMicBody: Desktop audio is dropped while the microphone is on.
settings.clipKeyHelp: Click to rebind, then press a key or a combo like Alt+F9. Escape cancels. Saved the moment you press it.
settings.hotkeysUnavailable: Gloaming cannot read your keyboard right now, so no hotkey will fire. Adding your user to the input group and logging back in usually fixes it.
settings.keyUnsupported: That key cannot be bound, try another
settings.errSaveKey: The key was captured but not saved
settings.clipPresetsHelp: Each key saves its own clip length. Double-tap any clip key to start or stop a session.
settings.blocklistHelp: One per line. Gloaming leaves its keys alone while a matching app is focused, for games that clip on the same keys. Matched against the window process and class, for example ggst.exe. Needs X11, Hyprland, Sway or Niri.
settings.tagWithGameHelp: Append the detected game to clip filenames, like Clip_2026-10-25_21-30-45_Overwatch-2.mp4. Uses the same game list as Rich Presence and the auto playlists.
settings.autoPlaylistHelp: When a known game is focused, file the clip into an auto playlist for it with its own colour.
settings.clipFilenameEmpty: That template renders to nothing, so the default naming will be used.
settings.portHelp: Port for the local share server
settings.publicLinkHelp: Share links that work outside your own network. Needs the cloudflared binary installed, otherwise links only work on your network.
settings.discordClientIdHelp: Optional. Leave empty to use Gloaming's own Discord application, or provide your own Application ID for custom branding.
settings.accentHelp: Tints the controls, the highlights and the ambient wash behind the app. Saved straight away, and shared clips pick it up too.
settings.effectsHelp: Motion and depth cost a GPU. Auto measures how fast frames arrive in this window and turns them down when it cannot keep up.
settings.effectsSoftware: This window is compositing in software, so effects are reduced.
settings.effectsSlow: Frames are arriving too slowly here, so effects are reduced.
settings.effectsKeepingUp: Frames are keeping up, so the full treatment is on.
settings.checkForUpdatesHelp: Ask GitHub once a day whether a newer Gloaming is out. Nothing about you or your clips is sent.
settings.checkNowHelp: Look straight away, ignoring the daily wait.
settings.upToDate: You are on the latest release
settings.bufferRaised: Buffer raised to {length} to cover your longest clip key
settings.restartBody: The sharing settings are saved, but the server only picks up a new port or tunnel setting when the daemon restarts.
settings.clipFilenameHelp: Leave empty for the default Clip_2026-10-25_21-30-45 naming. Use {n} for the clip number, {date}, {time}, and {game} (needs the toggle above). Clips are never overwritten.
settings.discordEnabledHelp: Puts "Clipping <Game> with Gloaming" on your Discord profile while a known game is focused. On by default, and window titles are never sent.
settings.discordGameIconsHelp: Shows the game's own Discord icon on your profile, with Gloaming's logo as a small badge. Gloaming looks the game up in Discord's public list of detectable games and caches the result. Off, or if a lookup fails, shows the plain Gloaming logo.
settings.discordCustomGamesHelp: One game per line: {format}. Matches are case-insensitive substrings checked against the focused window's process name and class. The bundled list already covers over 300 games.
settings.gsrArgsHelp: Appended to the recorder command as written. Example: {example}
settings.languageHelp: Gloaming is translated by the people who use it. If yours is missing or half done, the file to fill in is one JSON file: see docs/TRANSLATING.md.
settings.screenshotKeyHelp: Saves what is on screen as a picture, in the Images section. Unset by default. Screenshots are copied to the clipboard as well.
settings.imageDirectoryHelp: Where screenshots are written. Kept apart from clips so an image viewer is not indexing a folder of video files.
settings.shareDiscordFileHelp: On: the Share button copies the clip itself, shrunk to fit Discord's free upload limit, ready to paste into a message. Off: it copies the share link. Right-click Share for the other one either way.
settings.newSubtitle: Your setup. Your way to capture.
settings.liveReplayHelp: Browse your current replay buffer before saving a clip. Temporary recordings expire automatically. Applying this change restarts recording and clears the current replay buffer.
settings.replayShortcutHelp: Open the player over your game. Press again or Escape to return.
settings.basicIntroDescription: Your recording, audio and shortcuts. Everything you change most, in one place.
settings.sectionHint_recording: Choose how your screen is captured, encoded and processed.
settings.sectionHint_audio: Build your audio mix and choose how each source is recorded.
settings.sectionHint_hotkeys: Set up extra shortcuts, capture presets and application exclusions.
settings.sectionHint_storage: Keep your captures organized and manage the space they use.
settings.sectionHint_sharing: Choose how your clips are shared and who can reach them.
settings.sectionHint_discord: Customize how Gloaming connects with Discord.
settings.sectionHint_overlay: Configure what appears over your game and in your recordings.
settings.sectionHint_appearance: Make the interface feel like yours, from colors to visual effects.
settings.sectionHint_advanced: Manage application behavior and system-level preferences.
settings.recordingOverlayLive: Active in Live Replay — no overlay processing when saving.
settings.recordingOverlayFallback: Live overlay could not start. Inputs are currently added after saving, which takes longer.
settings.recordingOnlyHelp: Draw this overlay directly into recording and Live Replay while keeping it hidden during gameplay. Off by default. Adds continuous rendering work while enabled and avoids overlay processing when saving. Changing this option restarts the replay buffer. Embedded inputs cannot be hidden or removed, and no clean original is kept. If the capture plugin is unavailable, processing after saving is used instead.

whatsNew.title: What's new in Gloaming {version}
whatsNew.thanks: Thanks to {names} for their work on this release.

gameCapture.title: Record only the game
gameCapture.body: Turn on Game Capture in quick settings and Gloaming records just the game's window, so Discord and everything else stay out of your clips. It is off unless you turn it on.

discordShare.title: Share straight to Discord
discordShare.body: Right-click Share for a copy of the clip that fits Discord's free upload limit, ready to drag or paste. Settings, Sharing can make that what Share does. The editor can also export a Discord-sized file.

tray.title: Gloaming in the system tray
tray.body: On desktops with a system tray, closing the window now tucks Gloaming into the tray instead, and clicking the icon brings it back. Quit Gloaming from the tray menu stops recording too.

gameIcons.title: Your game's icon on Discord
gameIcons.body: Your Discord profile now shows the game's own icon while you play, with Gloaming's logo as a small badge. Turn it off in Settings, Discord.

steamNames.title: More games recognized
steamNames.body: Any game installed through Steam is now named in clips and on Discord, even when it is not on Gloaming's own list.

keyOverlay.title: Show your keys on screen
keyOverlay.body: A keyboard overlay shows the keys you press over your game, for streams and clips. Drag it where you want it or pick a corner. Gloaming can also keep the keys with each clip, to show in the viewer or add to an editor export. Both are off until you turn them on under Settings, Overlay.

trimCopy.title: Trimming keeps the original
trimCopy.body: Trim now saves your selection as a new clip and leaves the recording alone. Replacing the original is still there, and asks first.

trackVolume.title: A volume for each audio track
trackVolume.body: With separate audio tracks, each one now has its own volume under Settings, Audio, so a call or your mic can be heard over the game.

niri.title: Niri support
niri.body: Gloaming now sees which game you are playing on Niri, for clip names, game playlists and Discord.

flatpakGsr.title: The Flatpak gpu-screen-recorder
flatpakGsr.body: Gloaming can use the Flatpak build of gpu-screen-recorder, which keeps recording on the GPU on older NVIDIA cards that your system's FFmpeg has left behind. Choose it under Settings, Recording once it is installed.

languages.title: French, German and Brazilian Portuguese
languages.body: Gloaming is now available in French, German and Brazilian Portuguese. Pick a language in Settings, Appearance.

settingsUi.oneButtonTwoGesturesTap: One button, two gestures. Tap saves the last Clip duration instantly. Hold opens a menu to open the replay overlay or save the last 1, 2, 5, 10 minutes or the whole buffer. Pick with the D-pad, left stick or bumpers; you can let go once it appears. Tap again to close.
settingsUi.opensTheSaveLengthMenu: Opens the save-length menu on its own button, without the smart button's tap and hold: pick the last 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes, the whole buffer, or open the replay. Browse with the D-pad, left stick or bumpers. Press again to close.
settingsUi.savesTheLastClipDuration: Saves the last Clip duration selected in Capture & replay — seconds or minutes. This saves a video, without starting a recording session.
settingsUi.takeAStillImageWith: Take a still image with a controller button or combination. Triggers and the D-pad are supported. Executes when you release the buttons.
settingsUi.openOrCloseTheReplay: Open or close the replay overlay from your game. Assign a different button combination for each action. Button names show Xbox / PlayStation labels; face buttons follow physical positions.
settingsUi.openGloamingAutomaticallyWhenYou: Open Gloaming automatically when you log in, so clipping is ready before the game starts.
settingsUi.whenItOpensAtLogin: When it opens at login, start hidden in the tray.
settingsUi.minimizingTheWindowHidesIt: Minimizing the window hides it to the tray instead of the taskbar.
settingsUi.closingTheWindowHidesIt: Closing the window hides it to the tray and keeps recording. Use Quit in the tray menu to exit.
settingsUi.holdShiftWhileDraggingFor: Hold Shift while dragging for one-second adjustments. You can also click the duration to type an exact value.
settingsUi.showsAGamepadOverYour: Shows a gamepad over your game that lights up the buttons you press and follows the sticks and triggers, so recordings and streams show your inputs. It draws an Xbox or a PlayStation pad to match the controller you use.
settingsUi.autoFollowsTheControllerYou: Auto follows the controller you are pressing. Pick one to always show that drawing.
settingsUi.pickACornerOrPress: Pick a corner, or press Move and drag the pad anywhere on its screen. Press Done when it is where you want it.
settingsUi.openTheSaveLengthMenu: Open the save-length menu: pick the last 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes, the whole buffer, or open the replay. Press again to close. Arrow keys and Enter pick; Escape cancels.
settingsUi.noSystemTrayDetectedOn: No system tray detected on this desktop, so minimizing uses the taskbar.
settingsUi.noSystemTrayDetectedOn2: No system tray detected on this desktop, so closing the window quits Gloaming.
settingsUi.thisRecorderKeepsItsReplay: This recorder keeps its replay buffer on disk.
settingsUi.wfRecorderSupportsAutoH: wf-recorder supports Auto, H.264 NVENC, HEVC NVENC, H.264 VAAPI and software H.264. Other saved codecs use software H.264.
settingsUi.extraGsrArgumentsRequireGpu: Extra GSR arguments require GPU Screen Recorder.
settingsUi.setHowFarBackYou: Set how far back you can save, and where that history is kept.
settingsUi.chooseFrameRateColourDepth: Choose frame rate, colour depth, encoder and the saved file format.
settingsUi.chooseTheRecorderAndHow: Choose the recorder and how it follows your screen or window.
settingsUi.controlsVideoPlaybackInThe: Controls video playback in the app, independently of recording quality.
settingsUi.changesCouldNotBeSaved: Changes could not be saved. Your edits are still here.
settingsUi.navShortcutsHint: Every key and controller button, in one place
settingsUi.themeHelp: Dark, a soft grey light theme that is easy on the eyes, or follow your system. The replay overlay always stays dark.

ui.shiftSnapHint: Hold Shift to move in whole seconds
ui.jumpBackToLiveTo: Jump back to live to keep watching.
ui.yourReplayHistoryWillAppear: Your replay history will appear here as you record.
ui.revisitYourScreenFindThe: Revisit your screen, find the moment, and keep just the good part.
ui.pickALengthSaveA: Pick a length. Save a clip ending at the moment you’re watching.
ui.onlySavedClipsStayIn: Only saved clips stay in your library. Older replay history disappears automatically.
ui.yourSelectionExpiredResetIt: Your selection expired. Reset it to choose a newer moment.
ui.noReadableControllerConnectA: No readable controller. Connect a controller and press a button.
ui.restartGloamingToLoadController: Restart Gloaming to load controller status.
ui.connectedChooseAnActionBelow: Connected · Choose an action below to assign its buttons.
ui.noControllerDetectedConnectYour: No controller detected. Connect your controller to begin.
ui.chooseAPresetOrSelect: Choose a preset, or select Custom to tune the details.
ui.savedRecordingDefaultsExtraGsr: Saved recording defaults; extra GSR arguments take priority
ui.customizeBufferDurationInAdvanced: Customize buffer duration in Advanced settings
ui.liveReplayUsesThisBuffer: Live replay uses this buffer too. Changing it restarts recording and clears the current replay history.
ui.theseSettingsAreSharedWith: These settings are shared with Advanced recording. Choose an encoder, file format or storage location there.
ui.yourSavedClipsWillAppear: Your saved clips will appear here. Browse, organize and revisit your moments.
ui.theseFilesAreRemovedFrom: These files are removed from your disk and cannot be restored.
ui.savedOnYourDeviceYours: Saved on your device. Yours to keep.
ui.followingTheDisplayUnderYour: Following the display under your pointer
ui.yourScreenCapturedInThe: Your screen, captured in the background
ui.savedLocallyReadyWhenYou: Saved locally. Ready when you need it.
ui.exportWhileRecording: Gloaming is recording right now. Exporting will compete with the encoder for the GPU, so expect the game to stutter.
ui.replayBufferKeeps: Your replay buffer keeps the last {duration}.
ui.emptyMoments: Your saved moments will appear here. Press {hotkey} to keep one.
ui.holdButtons: {devices} · Hold your buttons together, then release.
ui.gsrOverrideThis: Extra GSR arguments ({args}) override this saved setting. Remove those arguments to use this control.
ui.gsrOverrideSome: Extra GSR arguments override some saved recording defaults. See the affected controls for details.
ui.depth10Supported: 10-bit uses HEVC NVENC and this wf-recorder build supports the required pixel format option.
ui.depth8Only: wf-recorder uses 8-bit here. 10-bit requires HEVC NVENC and a wf-recorder build with --pixel-format support.
ui.qualityNeedsGsr: Picture quality and fixed bitrate require GPU Screen Recorder.
ui.wfUsesCaptureSize: wf-recorder uses the capture size; picture size cannot be changed here.
ui.wfOwnFrameRate: wf-recorder controls its own frame rate.
ui.liveReplayLocks: Live replay uses GPU Screen Recorder, 8-bit H.264/AAC, MP4 clips and a disk buffer. Turn it off to change these settings. Your saved preferences are kept.
ui.noLivePlayback: This window does not support live replay playback.
ui.playbackInterrupted: Playback interrupted. Try Go live to reconnect.
ui.momentGone: That moment is no longer available. Choose a newer point.
ui.waitingFirstSeconds: Waiting for the first few seconds…
ui.noFullscreen: Fullscreen is not available in this window.
ui.qualityHelp: How much detail is kept, especially in fast motion. Higher looks sharper and makes bigger clips and a bigger buffer.
ui.bitrateHelp: The recording always uses this much data per second, whatever is on screen.
ui.historyHelp: How much of the past Gloaming keeps, ready to save. Longer history uses more memory or disk space.
ui.devicesLoadFailed: Some devices could not be loaded. Your saved selections are still available.
ui.appliesAfterSession: Settings will apply after the current session.
ui.lrStatusFail: Could not read live replay status.
ui.lrFinishSession: Finish the active recording session, then try again.
ui.qDefaultsNote: Saved defaults below; extra GSR arguments may change the actual recording.
ui.depthHelp: 10-bit looks smoother in gradients and is heavier. It needs a recent GPU.
ui.textSizeHelp: Scales the text and controls across the whole app, in every language. Arabic starts a little larger.
ui.moveKeyboard: Drag the keyboard to move it
ui.resizePanel: Drag to resize the panel, double-click to reset
